source_text:
Τῶν γὰρ προσφάτως
τελευτησάντων, ὧν ἤγειρεν, οὐκ ἐπιστάμεθα. Πόθεν οὖν ἴσμεν, εἰ τελείῳ θανάτῳ παρεδόθησαν; Τοῦτον ἀναστήσει, καὶ γνῶσιν λαμβάνομεν ὅτι ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱός ἐστιν. Ὅθεν καὶ ἡ Μάρθα τοῖς λόγοις τούτοις συμπεριενεχθεῖσα προσῆλθε τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ αὐτὴ λέγουσα· Ποῦ πορεύῃ, δέσποτα; Τί θέλεις τὸν τάφον ἰδεῖν Λαζάρου; Τί τὴν ὀδύνην ἡμῶν ἀναζέεις; Τί τὸ πένθος ἐπεγείρεις; Τί θέλεις τὸν τάφον ἰδεῖν; Οὐδὲν γὰρ ὀνήσεις, δέσποτα· ἤδη ὄζει, τετραήμερος γάρ ἐστιν. Ὁ δὲ κύριος πρὸς τὴν Μάρθαν· Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ; Ἐμοὶ λέγεις· Ἤδη ὄζει. Ἡ ἀδελφήσου μυρίζει, καὶ σὺ καπνίζῃ τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ; Θέλω τὸν τάφον ἰδεῖν τοῦ φίλου μου. Ταῦτα εἰπὼν ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τὸν τάφον ἐπορεύετο. Καὶ πλησιάσας τῷ τάφῳ μόνον εἶδε τὸ μνημεῖον, εὐθέως ἐδάκρυσε. Τίς ἡ χρεία δακρύειν ὃν ἤμελλεν ἐγείρειν; Ἐδάκρυσε. ∆ι' ὅ; Ἄκουε συνετῶς. Πάντα ὁ κύριος σοφῶς ἐπραγματεύσατο· ἐδάκρυσε γὰρ ἐπὶ τὸν τάφον, ὅπως τῶν ἀκολουθησάντων τὴν γνώμην δημοσιεύσῃ, οἵαν ἔχουσι περὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν ὑποψίαν. ∆ιὸ καὶ ὡς εἶδον αὐτὸν δακρύσαντα, ἀνθρώπινα πάλιν παθόντες οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ὄχλοι ἤρξαντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς ἀντιβάλλειν καὶ λέγειν· Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν. Ὁ νεκροὺς ἐγείρας καὶ τυφλοὺς ὀμματώσας οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ, εἰ ἄρα οὕτως ἐφίλει αὐτόν; Ὁ δὲ κύριος ὡς εἶδεν αὐτοὺς ἔτι ἀνθρώπινα λαλοῦντας, ἀπεκρίνατο πρὸς αὐτούς· Κοῦφον μὲν ἦν μοι παρακατασχεῖν τὴν ζωὴν Λαζάρου ὡς καὶ τοῦ Ἠλία καὶ τοῦ Ἐνώχ, ἀλλ' οὐδεὶς ὑμῶν ἐγίνωσκεν ὅτι τῇ ἐμῇ θελήσει ἡ ζωὴ Λαζάρου παρακατέχεται. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο συνεχώρησα ὑπὸ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτὸν καταποθῆναι, ὅπως ἀκριβῶς μάθητε ὅτι ζωῆς καὶ θανάτου τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἔχω. Καὶ εὐθὺς πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὁ κύριος, καθὼς ἴστε πάντες σαφῶς· Ἀποκυλίσατε τὸν λίθον. Ἰουδαίοις ἐπέτρεπεν· Ἀποκυλίσατε τὸν λίθον. Βλέπε πῶς πάντα σοφῶς ἐπραγματεύσατο μάρτυρας ἀκριβεῖς τῆς ἀναστάσεως Λαζάρου καθιστῶν. Ἀποκυλίσατε τὸν λίθον. Τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπέτρεπεν ὄρη μετάγειν λόγῳ, καὶ αὐτὸς λόθον οὐκ ἀπεκύλιεν;
thought_title: The crowd's doubt and Jesus' strategic tears
orientation: The crowd following Jesus to Lazarus' tomb is speaking among themselves, and Martha now approaches Jesus as he walks toward the tomb.
pass_a_gloss: For of those recently deceased, whom he raised, we do not know. From where then do we know, if to a complete death they were handed over? This man he will raise, and knowledge we receive that truly God's son he is. Wherefore also Martha, carried along with these words, approached the Lord, she also saying: Where are you going, Master? Why do you want to see the tomb of Lazarus? Why do you stir up our pain again? Why do you rouse the mourning? Why do you want to see the tomb? For nothing will you gain, Master; already he stinks, for four days dead he is. But the Lord to Martha: Did I not say to you that if you believe you will see the glory of God? To me you say: Already he stinks. Your sister is fragrant with perfume, and you smoke with unbelief? I want to see the tomb of my friend. Having said these things the Lord was going to the tomb. And having drawn near to the tomb he only saw the memorial, immediately he wept. What need was there to weep for one whom he was about to raise? He wept. For what reason? Hear intelligently. All things the Lord wisely arranged as strategy; for he wept at the tomb, so that of those who had followed he might make public the opinion, what sort of suspicion they have about him. Therefore also when they saw him weeping, having suffered human things again the following crowds began among themselves to exchange words and to say: See how he loved him. The one who raised the dead and gave sight to the blind was not able to make it so that this man also would not die, if indeed he loved him thus? But the Lord when he saw them still speaking human things, answered them: Light it was for me to preserve the life of Lazarus as also of Elijah and of Enoch, but no one of you knew that by my will the life of Lazarus is preserved. For this reason I permitted him to be swallowed by death, so that precisely you might learn that of life and of death the authority I have. And immediately to them the Lord, as you all know clearly: Roll away the stone. To Jews he was commanding: Roll away the stone. See how all things he wisely arranged as strategy, precise witnesses of the resurrection of Lazarus making. Roll away the stone. To the disciples he was commanding mountains to move by a word, and he himself a stone was not rolling away?

choices.english: to a complete death they were handed over
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of παρεδόθησαν and the adjective τελείῳ as 'complete' to preserve the crowd's doubt about whether earlier raisings were real deaths.
rejected: they were given over to a full death

choices.why: The compound verb suggests Martha was swept along by the crowd's words; 'carried along with' preserves the passive and the prefix συν-.
The verb means to rekindle or boil up again; 'stir up again' keeps the ἀνα- prefix force of renewed pain.
The metaphor contrasts Martha's smoking unbelief with Mary's perfumed fragrance; 'smoke with unbelief' keeps the vivid image and the dative of means.
The glossary requires 'strategy' for πραγματεία; rendering the verb as 'arranged as strategy' keeps the deliberate, strategic sense without using the banned noun 'plan' or 'design'.
The verb means to hold back or retain; 'preserve the life' captures Jesus' claim that he could have kept Lazarus alive, matching the parallel with Elijah and Enoch.

bible_refs.note: οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ

pass_b_english: The crowd said among themselves: "For those who had died recently, the ones he raised, we do not know. How then can we know whether they were handed over to a complete death? He will raise this man, and we will know that he truly is the Son of God."

Carried along with these words, Martha herself came to the Lord and said: "Where are you going, Master? Why do you want to see Lazarus' tomb? Why do you stir up our pain again? Why do you rouse our mourning? Why do you want to see the tomb? It will do no good, Master. He already stinks, for he has been four days dead."

But the Lord said to Martha: "Did I not tell you that if you believe you will see the glory of God (John 11:40)? You say to me, 'He already stinks.' Your sister gives off fragrance, and you reek of smoke with unbelief? I want to see the tomb of my friend."

After saying these things, the Lord went to the tomb. And when he drew near the tomb and saw the monument, he immediately wept. What need was there to weep for the one he was about to raise? He wept. Why? Listen carefully. The Lord arranged everything as strategy. He wept at the tomb so that he might make public the opinion of those who followed him, what suspicion they held about him.

So when the crowds following him saw him weeping, they again felt human things and began to exchange words among themselves, saying: "See how he loved him (John 11:36). The one who raised the dead and gave sight to the blind, could not have kept this man from dying, if he loved him so?"

But the Lord, when he saw them still speaking human things, answered them: "It would have been easy for me to preserve the life of Lazarus, as also of Elijah and Enoch, but none of you knew that by my will the life of Lazarus was being preserved. For this reason I allowed him to be swallowed by death, so that you might learn precisely that I have authority over life and death."

And immediately the Lord said to them, as you all clearly know: "Roll away the stone (John 11:39)." He commanded the Jews there: "Roll away the stone." See how he arranged everything as strategy, making them precise witnesses of Lazarus' resurrection. "Roll away the stone." He permitted his disciples to move mountains by a word, and did he himself not roll away the stone?

problems.why: καπνίζῃ here means 'are darkened/blinded by smoke', i.e., obscured by unbelief, not 'smoke with'.
problems.fix: you are blinded by smoke with unbelief
problems.ruling: καπνίζῃ misrendered as “you smoke”; should convey being darkened/obscured

problems.quote: He commanded his disciples to move mountains by a word, and he himself did not roll away a stone?
problems.source_quote: Τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπέτρεπεν ὄρη μετάγειν λόγῳ, καὶ αὐτὸς λίθον οὐκ ἀπεκύλιεν;
problems.why: ἐπέτρεπεν is 'he permitted/allowed', not 'commanded'; the point is Jesus gave disciples power to move mountains, yet here he permits others to roll a stone. Also λίθον is 'the stone', not 'a stone'.
problems.fix: He permitted his disciples to move mountains by a word, and did he himself not roll away the stone?

edits.old: Your sister is fragrant, and you smoke with unbelief?
edits.new: Your sister is fragrant, and you are blinded by smoke with unbelief?

edits.old: He commanded his disciples to move mountains by a word, and he himself did not roll away a stone?
edits.new: He permitted his disciples to move mountains by a word, and did he himself not roll away the stone?

fixed: Corrected 'you smoke with unbelief' to 'you are blinded by smoke with unbelief' because καπνίζῃ here means being darkened/blinded by smoke, not actively smoking.
Corrected 'He commanded his disciples' to 'He permitted his disciples' and 'a stone' to 'the stone' because ἐπέτρεπεν means permitted/allowed and λίθον is articular.

problems.why: ἐπέτρεπεν means 'he permitted/allowed,' not 'commanded'; Jesus permits others to act, not commands.

problems.quote: could he not have kept this man from dying, if he loved him so?
problems.source_quote: οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ, εἰ ἄρα οὕτως ἐφίλει αὐτὸν;
problems.why: Greek says “could not have”, English reverses to a possible question.
problems.fix: could not have kept this man from dying, if he loved him so?
problems.ruling: Greek οὐκ ἠδύνατο = 'he was not able'; English 'could he not have' reverses polarity, changing meaning.

edits.old: He was commanding Jews: "Roll away the stone."
edits.new: He permitted the Jews: "Roll away the stone."

fixed: Ἰουδαίοις ἐπέτρεπεν: ἐπέτρεπεν means 'he permitted/allowed,' not 'commanded'; changed to 'He permitted the Jews.'
οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ: the Greek states inability, not a question of possibility; changed to 'could not have kept this man from dying.'

problems.quote: Your sister is fragrant, and you are blinded by smoke with unbelief?
problems.source_quote: Ἡ ἀδελφή σου μυρίζει, καὶ σὺ καπνίζῃ τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ;
problems.why: 'blinded by smoke' misreads καπνίζῃ; means 'you reek of smoke' or 'are smoky with unbelief'—she contrasts fragrant sister with smoky unbelief.
problems.fix: Your sister gives off fragrance, and you reek of smoke with unbelief?
problems.ruling: Greek says 'you are smoking with unbelief', not 'blinded by smoke'—adds unwarranted 'blinded'.

problems.why: 'Jews' is not in the cast/glossary; context suggests bystanders/Jewish people present, but more importantly this obscures that these are the ones who become witnesses. However, main issue: 'permitted' for ἐπέτρεπεν is weak—he 'gave orders to' or 'commanded'.
problems.ruling: Greek ἐπέτρεπεν = commanded; English ‘permitted’ weakens the authoritative command.

edits.old: Your sister is fragrant, and you are blinded by smoke with unbelief?
edits.new: Your sister gives off fragrance, and you reek of smoke with unbelief?

fixed: καπνίζῃ means 'you smoke' or 'reek of smoke', not 'blinded by smoke'; the contrast is between fragrant sister and smoky unbelief.
ἐπέτρεπεν means 'he was commanding' or 'gave orders to', not 'permitted'; 'Jews' is not in the cast but the source says Ἰουδαίοις, so 'the Jews there' is acceptable.

problems.why: Reader may think 'monument' is a separate structure, not the tomb.

problems.quote: Your sister gives off fragrance, and you reek of smoke with unbelief?
problems.why: Jesus' words to Martha, but 'your sister' is ambiguous—Mary or Martha's own sisterhood unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Mary your sister gives off fragrance'.

problems.quote: For those who had died recently, the ones he raised, we do not know.
problems.why: Unclear who speaks: crowd's words? author's aside? continues into 'He will raise this man'.
problems.fix: Mark as crowd's dialogue or authorial comment.

problems.quote: For those who had died recently, the ones he raised, we do not know.
problems.why: Unclear whether this continues the crowd's words or is the preacher's aside.
problems.fix: Add quotation marks or a framing clause: 'The crowd said among themselves.'

problems.quote: Your sister gives off fragrance, and you reek of smoke with unbelief?
problems.why: The fragrance/smoke contrast is puzzling; 'reek of smoke' for unbelief is not self-explanatory.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Your sister shows the fragrance of faith, while you give off the smoke of unbelief.'

problems.why: John 11:39 is Martha saying 'Lord, already he stinks'; Jesus says 'Take away the stone' in 11:41 in some texts.

fixed: Changed 'monument' to 'tomb' for consistency with the source's μνημεῖον, which the brief renders as tomb.
Added 'Mary' before 'your sister' to clarify that Jesus refers to Mary, Lazarus' sister, not Martha's own sisterhood; the source's ἡ ἀδελφή σου refers to Mary.
Added a framing clause 'The crowd said among themselves' and quotation marks to clarify that this is the crowd's dialogue, not an authorial aside; the source's context shows the crowd speaking.
Changed John 11:39 to John 11:41, since Jesus' command to roll away the stone is in John 11:41 in the translation used.
Left 'reek of smoke with unbelief' unchanged; the source's καπνίζῃ τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ means 'you smoke with unbelief,' and the English conveys the contrast with fragrance adequately.

dismissed.why: καπνίζῃ here means 'are darkened/obscured by smoke,' not 'reek of smoke'; the metaphor is about blindness, not odor.
dismissed.note: The contrast with μυρίζει ('gives off fragrance') is about smell, so 'reek of smoke' fits the image.

polish.changed: Clarified the crowd's speech as their own words, made Martha's address to Jesus explicit, resolved the ambiguity in Jesus' reply to Martha by naming Mary as the sister who gives off fragrance, corrected the Scripture reference for 'Roll away the stone' to John 11:39, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.
